newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond rally halted by Tankan jump.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond rally halted by Tankan jump.

text.p: *An early rally in Australian bond futures was halted after a stronger than expected Japanese Tankan survey, although the local market was seen as over-extended in early thin trade.
*Market now looks to U.S. for next direction.

An early rally in Australian bond futures was all but wiped out after a stronger than expected Japanese Tankan survey raised the possibility of higher Japanese interest rates and narrow differentials to Australia.
"That's the implication from the data and it's caused a bit of a wobble in our market. But our market had been looking a bit over-extended in a thin market," one trader said.
The September 10-year bond futures contract had spiked to 92.990 before the Tankan survey, but was subsequently rowed back to around unchanged.
The second quarter Tankan survey showed the key big manufacturers' diffusion index at plus seven after plus 2 in March and when forecasts had focussed on a small fall.

Traders said that while the data had knocked back the local market, it was finding support at the lows, although turnover remains uninspired in the absence of local domestic indicators, and ahead of next week's monetary policy making meetings in Australia and the United States.
The initial firm tone followed a more stable U.S. Treasury market after a reasonably well received two year note sale. The U.S. faces May durable goods orders later on Wednesday.
